name: Story and Structure
kicker: UI/UX design · data engineering · brand reference
lede: How the studio looks and why. Deep forest green holds the structure, blush pink carries the story, and ink and orchid show the data underneath. We design the interface and build the pipeline behind it, so the brand has to feel human and exact at the same time.

brand.title: A good story needs a sound structure
brand.lede: The name is the method. Every project starts with the story a person needs to follow, then builds the structure (the interface, the data model, the pipeline) that keeps it true. Each brand color has one of those jobs.

personality.caption: How a client should feel reading a proposal, or an engineer opening the handoff file.

names: Story and Structure, with "and" spelled out and in lowercase
S&S, only where space is tight: favicons, avatars, file prefixes
Tokens have no prefix (--forest, --primary). Files start with story-structure-

color_rules.forest: Primary buttons, active nav, links and focus rings. In dark mode it lightens to sage and takes dark text.
color_rules.blush: One thread per view (see Signature). Fails as text in light mode at 1.3:1, so it is only ever a fill under dark text.
color_rules.orchid: Tags, diagram links and the third chart series. White text passes on it only just (4.9:1), so keep button text at 16px or larger.
color_rules.ink: Info notices, code accents and the first chart series. The heatmap ramp is built from it.

charts.bars_label: Example data · pipeline runs per month
rules: Series order is fixed: ink, forest, orchid. Colors follow the thing shown, never its rank.
Blush is never a chart series. It marks the one insight a chart is about, as an annotation band.
Axis labels, values and legends use text greys, never the series color.
Failed runs use the error red, always with a label.

signature.title: One story thread per view
signature.lede: Blush is the story. Each view gets one thread: a single highlighted phrase, one callout or one soft section. Everything else stays forest, ink and neutral, so the thread is what the eye follows.

type.title: Fraunces for the story, IBM Plex for the structure
type.lede: A soft serif for headlines and pull quotes, where the studio speaks. IBM Plex Sans for interface and body text, and Plex Mono for code, SQL and numbers in tables. The two Plex faces share proportions, so data and prose sit together cleanly.

display.chars: Aa Bb Cc · Research that ships
display.use: Headlines, section titles and pull quotes. Never below 20px.

ui.use: Interface, body text, buttons and KPI values.

mono.use: Code, SQL, column names and token names.

scale.label: Pull quote
scale.sample: “The numbers on screen are the numbers in the warehouse.”

scale.label: Body
scale.sample: We design the interface and build the data underneath it, so what people see on screen and what's in the warehouse always agree.

scale.label: Code
scale.sample: SELECT project, COUNT(*) FROM fct_events GROUP BY 1

layout.title: A 12-column grid on a 4px base
layout.lede: Marketing pages and case studies use a top bar over a 12-column grid, up to 1200px wide with 24px gutters. Product work and dashboards switch to a 260px sidebar. Below 768px everything stacks to one column.
facts: 0.5rem on buttons, inputs and notices. Cards use 12px, pills 999px.
12 columns, 24px gutters, 1200px max. Case-study text runs 7 columns wide.

input.label: Work email
input.help: We reply within two working days.
input.error: Enter an email address with an @.

notices.info: The pipeline refreshes every hour. Last run 14:00.
notices.highlight: Load time dropped from 40 seconds to 2 after the rebuild.
notices.error: Sync failed. Check the warehouse connection, then try again.

always: Pair the error red with an icon and a word ("Sync failed"), never color alone.
Blush is a fill, never text. Put the darkest neutral on it.
Keep a legend or direct labels on any chart with two or more series.
Focus rings: a 2px outline in the forest text color, 2px offset.
